subject: DeltaHealth — hosted API volume sanity check & pricing next steps

From: Avery Freeman <avery@deltahealth.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: traffic shape and early numbers

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. A few quick notes from our side on the traffic shape so you can sanity-check pricing before you put something formal together:

- Rough monthly token estimate (product queries only): ~1,200,000,000 tokens/month
- Average tokens per request: ~280 tokens
- Peak traffic window: weekday mornings (08:00-10:00 PT) — peak observed/requested shape ~60,000 tokens/sec (short bursts up to ~75k for 2-3 min)
- Typical daily steady-state tokens/sec: ~8,500
- Ballpark budget range the team is comfortable with: $8 - $15 per 1M tokens; internal target is $10-12/1M if we can get predictable latency and an SLA
- Timeline: procurement runway targets a PO within 4-6 weeks if pricing and SOC/controls check out

Can you confirm those numbers look feasible on Redwood hosted and send a short cost sketch (pilot vs production bands) + next steps for procurement? Happy to share a token sample file if helpful.

— Avery
Avery Freeman
Sr. Product Manager, DeltaHealth
avery@deltahealth.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: traffic shape and early numbers

Thanks Avery — appreciate the clear shape. Quick recap + cost sketch below (sharing with Jordan & Karthik for capacity/ops input):

Summary of the numbers you shared:
- Monthly tokens: 1,200,000,000 (1.2B)
- Avg tokens / request: 280
- Peak tokens/sec: 60,000 (short bursts to 75k)
- Budget range: $8-15 per 1M tokens, target $10-12/1M

Cost sketches (simple arithmetic):
- At $8 / 1M tokens -> 1,200M / 1M = 1200 units -> 1200 * $8 = $9,600 / month
- At $10 / 1M -> 1200 * $10 = $12,000 / month
- At $12 / 1M -> 1200 * $12 = $14,400 / month

Notes on capacity and SLOs:
- Peak 60k tokens/sec translates into GPU scaling requirements for hosted (we typically route to multi-tenant pools with burst capacity). To guarantee 99th percentile latency during bursts we recommend either a reserved "burst-capacity" band or a short canary capacity reservation. Jordan + Karthik: will follow up with rough instance count and latency SLO trade-offs in parallel.

Attachments: I attached a quick token profile template (deltahealth-token-profile.csv) — if you can populate or confirm samples, that will help us firm up the slab recommendation.

Proposed next steps (suggested):
1) You confirm the monthly token baseline (and whether 1.2B includes occasional batch jobs)
2) We propose a 3-month pilot slab (we'll draft SOW) with an optional ramp to production slab if you hit >1B tokens/mo
3) Procurement contact + PO timeline (we can align DocuSign SOW flow to your procurement needs)
4) I’ll send a short pricing spreadsheet with three slabs (pilot / production band / committed band) and expected monthly cost at $8/$10/$12/ $15 per 1M tokens

If the numbers above look right I'll turn the spreadsheet & SOW draft around by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Subject: DeltaHealth: updated numbers acknowledged + proposed pilot pricing

Great — thanks for the correction, Avery. Confirmed for the pilot scope:
- User-facing monthly tokens: 720,000,000 tokens/month
- Peak tokens/sec (user-facing): 40,000 (short bursts up to ~50k)
- Procurement contact: procurement@deltahealth.com
- Budget target: $10 / 1M tokens (preferred)

Pricing proposal (pilot-focused, non-binding):
- Pilot slab (3 months, reserved pilot capacity): 720M tokens/mo @ $12 / 1M -> $8,640 / month
- Production ramp (committed 12-month): 1.2B tokens/mo @ $10 / 1M -> $12,000 / month (example band once you expand beyond pilot)
- Committed enterprise band (2B+/mo) -> $8 / 1M (negotiated)

Why recommend the pilot slab at $12/1M vs immediate $10/1M:
- Pilot includes burst-capacity buffer and priority routing during peak 40k/sec windows; it also includes a 72-hour incident response SLA for the pilot period and dedicated onboarding support to validate latency SLOs.
- If performance and reliability meet your expectations, we will convert to the production committed band at $10/1M (or lower depending on commitment).

Attachments included: redwood-proposed-slab-pricing.xlsx (breakdown by slab & incremental cost), SOW-DeltaHealth-Redwood-3mo.pdf (pilot SOW draft). I also attached the token profile we requested (deltahealth-token-profile.csv) — thanks for sharing the sample earlier.

Next concrete steps:
1) I’ll share a DocuSign SOW draft + HubSpot deal link for internal tracking (links below).
2) Procurement to review SOW; Rafael to follow up on pricing/capacity questions within 48 hours.
3) Schedule a 30-min onboarding sync with our Solutions team the week after SOW signature to validate peak handling & test traffic profile.
